recommendations: In appropriately selected individuals, CRT reduces morbidity and mortality, improves cardiac function, and enhances quality of life.
Implantation of CRT is not recommended if QRS duration is <130 ms (Echo-CRT trial and an IPD meta-analysis suggest possible harm when QRS <130 ms).
content.evidence_level_summary: Multiple randomized trials and IPD meta-analyses referenced (eg, CARE-HF, COMPANION, MADIT-II, RAFT, MADIT-CRT, REVERSE, BLOCK-HF) support CRT benefits in selected populations.
trial_findings_and_notes: CARE-HF, COMPANION compared CRT with medical therapy; many CRT studies compared CRT-D with ICD; a few compared CRT-P with backup pacing.
In CARE-HF at baseline 25% of patients had resting heart rate <60 b.p.m.
In MADIT-II, 35% of those who died with an ICD died suddenly despite protection from brady- and tachyarrhythmia.

LVEF_thresholds_for_inclusion_in_trials.note: Relatively few patients with LVEF of 35–40% have been randomized; an IPD meta-analysis suggests no diminution of CRT effect in this group.

predictors_of_response: Extent of reverse remodelling is an important mechanism of CRT benefit.
Patients with HFrEF of ischaemic aetiology have less improvement in LV function due to myocardial scar and are less likely to undergo favourable remodelling.
Women may be more likely to respond than men, possibly due to smaller body and heart size.
QRS width predicts CRT response and was an inclusion criterion in randomized trials; QRS morphology (eg, LBBB) has also been related to beneficial response.
Patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB) morphology are more likely to respond favourably; evidence is less certain for non-LBBB morphology.

There is debate whether QRS duration or QRS morphology is the main predictor; after accounting for QRS duration, limited evidence that morphology or disease aetiology influences CRT effect on morbidity/mortality.
practical_guidance: Select patients based on LVEF thresholds used in major trials (commonly ≤35%).
Avoid CRT implantation when QRS duration is <130 ms due to potential harm.
Consider ischaemic aetiology, QRS duration, and LBBB morphology when predicting likelihood of response; women may derive greater benefit.

abbreviations_found.QRS: Q, R, and S waves of an ECG
abbreviations_found.HFrEF: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
